name: Lisch Corneal Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of band-shaped microcysts in the corneal epithelium observed on slit-lamp examination
Mild visual disturbance or decreased visual acuity related to corneal epithelial changes
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of band-shaped microcysts in the corneal epithelium with mild visual disturbance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical based on slit-lamp findings; genetic testing is not routinely performed.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic band-like distribution of microcysts in the corneal epithelium
Usually mild and non-progressive visual disturbance

common.notes: Surface irregularities noted on slit-lamp examination
Light sensitivity reported in some patients

occasional.notes: Episodes of corneal epithelial breakdown causing pain
Subtle stromal changes may be present
May contribute to ocular surface discomfort

rare.notes: Rarely observed in advanced or complicated cases
Extremely rare, usually due to secondary complications

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing band-shaped microcystic epithelial lesions
In vivo confocal microscopy showing microcystic epithelial changes
genetic: No specific gene mutation identified; possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Corneal sensitivity testing may be normal or mildly reduced

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse microcysts throughout corneal epithelium rather than band-shaped

redFlags: Signs of corneal infection or ulceration
references: Krachmer JH, Mannis MJ, Holland EJ. Cornea. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2011.
Weiss JS, Møller HU, Lisch W, et al. The IC3D classification of the corneal dystrophies. Cornea. 2008;27(2):S1-S83.
Klintworth GK. Corneal dystrophies. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2009;4:7.
